classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the circle's centre as the diameter's midpoint, then reverse the midpoint relationship to recover both coordinates of X.

content.prompt: The circle has diameter $XY$ and centre $Z$. What are the coordinates of $X$?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7, circle diagram beneath the prompt
spec.description: Unshaded circle with double-ended coordinate axes, no scale ticks, numeric origin label 0, marked centre Z and diameter endpoints X and Y. Ordinary source blue circle and diameter are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: The circle has centre Z=(1,1), radius sqrt(13), and diameter through Y=(4,-1). The unlabelled coordinates of X are represented geometrically without printing their values.
spec.answerVisibility: Student-visible givens and geometry only; X has no coordinate annotation.

answer.short:
$X(-2,3)$

Double the centre coordinates, then subtract the coordinates of Y.
answer.worked:
The midpoint of the diameter is the centre.
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{x_X+4}{2}&=1\\
x_X+4&=2\\
x_X&=-2\\
\frac{y_X+(-1)}{2}&=1\\
y_X-1&=2\\
y_X&=3
\end{align*}$$
$X(-2,3)$.
